title: Why Java avoids explicit C/C++-style pointers
answer: Java hides ordinary raw pointers to keep the language and runtime safer, simpler, more portable, and compatible with managed memory. Object references let programs reach objects without exposing address arithmetic or manual dereferencing. Because the JVM and garbage collector control object memory, application code does not need to depend on fixed raw addresses. Removing normal pointer arithmetic also avoids many classes of accidental memory corruption and dangling-pointer bugs common in unmanaged code. Java can still interact with native memory through specialized APIs and native interop, but that is deliberately separate from everyday object-reference syntax.
